theater: 上埃及提比斯與亞歷山大港

battle.name: 巴蘇斯戰爭
battle.theater: 上埃及提比斯與亞歷山大港
battle.brief: 公元494年末，亞歷山大港的帝國派把巴蘇斯推上皇位，與提比斯的狄奧多西派開火。提比斯派倚僧院武裝沿尼羅河谷北進，帝國派以禁衛軍與海運守住三角洲港口，交戰自赫爾莫波利斯打到亞歷山大城下，巴蘇斯最後在卡爾刻冬被處決。卡面月牙劍已退出戰陣，此役上手的是羅馬短劍、長矛與鎖甲。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 巴蘇斯戰爭是五世紀末羅馬帝國埃及行省內部的一場內戰，交戰雙方都不是外敵，而是同一個帝國體系內的兩派：北岸亞歷山大港的「帝國派」與南面提比斯的「提比斯派」（教會史上稱狄奧多西派）。帝國派以亞歷山大城的市民上層、墨里西安派宗主教狄奧斯庫魯斯所率的教會，以及掌握行省稅收、司法與港口的羅馬官僚為骨幹，其合法性來自君士坦丁堡的東羅馬皇帝；提比斯派則以亞歷山大港主教狄奧多西為精神核心，由非神職出身的領袖奧林匹多羅斯實際調動上埃及的僧院、村落武裝與農戶，在自赫爾莫波利斯到賽伊尼的尼羅河谷上游建立了獨立的武裝經濟。衝突的直接背景是484年東方禁衛軍總督弗拉維烏斯·巴蘇斯在亞歷山大港對米阿斐西特（沙伊特）教眾的屠殺，以及次年巴蘇斯本人被亞歷山大港反對者殺死所激起的連鎖報復；其後東羅馬更換總督、皇帝阿納斯塔修斯一世於491年即位，迫害與反迫害交替進行，亞歷山大與提比斯之間的軍力對比遂在494年被一場擁立行為引爆。帝國一方的正式指揮系統是埃及邊界統帥（comes limitis Aegypti）與亞歷山大港的禁衛軍分遣隊，另有海軍分遣隊控制河口；提比斯一方則沒有常備建制，靠僧院、村落與河運臨時集結。
countriesEn: The War of the Bassus was a civil war fought inside the Roman province of Egypt in the late fifth century, and neither side was a foreign enemy: both were factions of the same imperial system. On one side stood the imperial party of Alexandria on the north coast, built on the city's Greek-speaking upper class, the Melkite church under the patriarch Dioscorus, and the Roman officials who controlled the province's taxes, its courts and its harbour; its legitimacy came from the eastern emperor at Constantinople. On the other stood the Theban party, called the Theodosian party in church history, centred on the bishop of Alexandria Theodosius as its spiritual core and actually led on the ground by Olympiodorus, a layman who could mobilise the monasteries, the village militias and the peasants of Upper Egypt, giving the party an armed economy of its own along the Nile from Hermopolis to Syene. The immediate background was the massacre of the Miaphysite (Sha'ite) faithful in Alexandria in 484 by the praetorian prefect of the East, Flavius Bassus, and the chain of reprisals set off when Bassus himself was killed by the Alexandrians the following year; the empire then changed prefects, the emperor Anastasius I came to the throne in 491, persecution and counter-persecution alternated, and the balance of force between Alexandria and Thebes was finally overturned in 494 by a proclamation of an emperor. The imperial side's formal chain of command ran through the comes limitis Aegypti and the detachments of the imperial guard at Alexandria, with a detachment of the fleet controlling the river mouths; the Theban side had no standing establishment at all and could only raise its men from monasteries, villages and river transport.
people: 留下姓名的多數屬於提比斯派與朝廷。奧林匹多羅斯是這場戰爭真正的軍事主角：他是上埃及的平信徒與學者，本以教師與醫生的身分生活，後來成為狄奧多西派在提比斯一線的實際首腦，組織僧團武裝、指揮河谷內的攻勢，最後在495年前後被自己一方與敵方的衝突捲入而遇害；六世紀時查士丁尼在《新律》的序言裡還特意稱揚他的學問與名望，可見當時的敵我雙方都清楚他的分量。狄奧多西是亞歷山大港主教，482年至566年在任，本人在戰爭中偏向退守與妥協，沒有親自帶兵，但正是他這位宗主教的存在，讓提比斯派有了對抗亞歷山大城宗主教派與君士坦丁堡的旗幟。阿納斯塔修斯一世自491年在位至518年，他拒絕承認巴蘇斯的帝號，先以帝國正軍討伐亞歷山大港的擁立者，戰局轉向後又轉而清算提比斯派，末了把巴蘇斯押到卡爾刻冬處決。被推舉為皇帝的巴蘇斯本人留下的記錄極少，只知他是羅馬人，可能與484年遇害的總督同族，姓名或為當時人給他的稱號，他沒有留下任何軍令或文書。亞歷山大港一方的宗主教狄奧斯庫魯斯，486年至496年在任，是墨里西安派的領袖，在教會史上常被批評為向帝國派低頭。此外，先後被派往埃及的禁衛軍總督魯弗魯斯也在亞歷山大港的黨爭中捲入極深，最終被解職並處死，編年史正是以他之死作為戰局轉折的記號。主要史料是米蒂利尼的Zacharias所撰編年史、《亞歷山大教宗史》（Historia Patrum）與後來開羅的John of Nikiu的編年史，三者的立場都偏袒提比斯派，讀數時要留一分心眼。
peopleEn: Most of the names that survive belong to the Theban party and to the court. Olympiodorus is the real military protagonist of the war: a layman and scholar from Upper Egypt who had lived as a teacher and a physician, he became in practice the head of the Theodosian party on the Theban front, organised the armed monastic squads and directed the offensive up and down the valley, and was killed amid the collision between his own side and its enemies around 495. In the sixth century Justinian still singled him out for praise in the preface to one of his Novellas, which shows that both sides then understood exactly how much weight he carried. Theodosius, bishop of Alexandria from 482 to 566, was the spiritual authority of the Theban party; he stayed defensive during the fighting and led no troops in person, but it was precisely his standing as bishop that gave the Theban party a banner to raise against the Melkite establishment of Alexandria and against Constantinople. Anastasius I reigned from 491 to 518. He refused to recognise Bassus as emperor, first sent the regular imperial army against the men who had acclaimed him at Alexandria, turned his hand against the Theban party once the situation shifted, and finally had Bassus executed at Chalcedon. Bassus himself left almost nothing in the record: we know only that he was a Roman, possibly of the same family as the prefect killed in 484, and that the name Bassus may have been what the Alexandrians actually used for him; he left no orders and no writings. Dioscorus of Alexandria, Melkite patriarch from 486 to 496, led the other side and is often criticised in church history for bowing to the imperial party. The prefects of the East sent to Egypt in turn, among them the eunuch Rufinus, were also drawn deep into the Alexandrian faction fight, and Rufinus was eventually dismissed and put to death; the chronicler duly uses his death as the marker of the turning point. The main sources are the chronicle of Zacharias of Mytilene, the Historia Patrum, and later the chronicle of John of Nikiu; all three lean towards the Theban party, so their figures have to be read with a grain of salt.
kits: 先要說清楚一件容易被誤讀的事：卡面上的這把埃及月牙劍並沒有出現在這場戰爭裡。它是埃及自古王朝以來就有的近身兵器，青銅質、單刃、刃口開在凸面，彎如新月，砍進人身或盾牌之後不必回抽；到第十八王朝它已讓位給更省力的直刃短劍與新興的鐵器，到公元五世紀更是只存在於收藏與神廟器物之中，實戰陣上早已無人再握。所以本役真正上手的是別的兵器。帝國派與朝廷正軍用的是晚期羅馬裝備：短劍（gladius）與長劍（spatha）、匕首（pugio）、長矛（hasta）與標槍（para）、橢圓大盾（scutum）、環扣鎖子甲（lorica hamata）與鱗甲（lorica squamata）、頭盔（galea）、帶飾件的劍帶（cingulum）；輔兵改用橢圓小盾，騎兵以長劍配盾，投石手（slingarii）與弓箭手分隊作戰，軍中亦有弩砲（onager、arcuballista）一類的擲射器械與攻城塔、撞槌，只是這類器械在埃及內戰的記載裡不常出現。提比斯派的武裝則是另一套樣貌：僧侶與村落武裝的近戰兵多持本地鍛造的鐵刃短刀、削尖的木矛與棒，配小圓盾或藤編護具，弓兵用埃及本地製的弓，缺甲就以皮甲、粗麻衣與頭巾充數，必要時把農具改成兵器。雙方共通的後勤裝備是尼羅河上的駁船與貨船、駱駝與驢隊、磨坊小麥、大麥、鹽與椰棗，以及把糧食從三角洲運往提比斯、或從提比斯運往亞歷山大港的船隊。
kitsEn: One thing has to be said first, because it is easy to misread: the Egyptian khopesh on the card did not appear in this war. It was a close-combat weapon Egypt had had since the Old Kingdom, bronze, single-edged, its edge on the convex side, curved like a new moon, and it did not have to be pulled back after it bit into a body or a shield; by the Eighteenth Dynasty it had already been pushed aside by the more efficient straight-edged sword and by new ironwork, and by the fifth century CE it survived only in collections and in temple treasure, with nobody on a battlefield still holding one. The weapons actually in hand here were others. The imperial party and the regular army used the late Roman kit: the short sword (gladius) and the long sword (spatha), the dagger (pugio), the spear (hasta) and the javelin (para), the oval shield (scutum), mail (lorica hamata) and scale armour (lorica squamata), the helmet (galea), and the sword-belt (cingulum) with its fittings; auxiliaries carried smaller oval shields, cavalry fought with the spatha and a shield, sling infantry (slingarii) and archer detachments formed their own units, and the army also had onager and arcuballista-type artillery, siege towers and battering rams, though such engines hardly appear in the accounts of an Egyptian civil war. The Theban party's equipment looked quite different: the close-fighting men drawn from the monasteries and the villages mostly carried locally forged iron knives, sharpened wooden spears and clubs, with small round shields or wickerwork protection; their archers used locally made bows, and where armour was lacking they made do with leather, coarse linen and head-cloths, turning farm tools into weapons when they had to. The logistics common to both sides were the lighters and cargo boats on the Nile, camel and donkey trains, milled wheat and barley, salt and dates, and the grain fleets that carried food from the Delta to Thebes or from Thebes to the harbour of Alexandria.
tactics: 這場內戰的形狀，是由兩套完全不對稱的戰爭體系拼出來的。帝國派的基本戰術是「以海峽與河道換時間」：亞歷山大港是地中海的深水港，帝國的穀船隊每年冬季由此出發，沿塞浦路斯與小亞細亞海峽北上；守住港口，就守住了羅馬的埃及收入。正軍沿尼羅河與運河推進，在渡口、橋樑與城鎮設卡封鎖，用海軍巡弋河口，切斷提比斯派的鹽與小麥流向；作戰以據點為主，步步為營，等待提比斯派自己撞上來。提比斯派的戰術是另一回事：他們沒有常備軍，靠僧院與村落作節點，以游擊與夜襲為主，隊伍沿河谷南北移動，善用渡船與本地嚮導，在自己熟悉的村落裡作戰，把僧院與教堂改造成堡壘，用投石、標槍與房屋作掩體；人數上以僧侶加農戶的混合隊伍壓過對方，但裝備與訓練不足，久戰與正面衝鋒都吃虧。編年史提到提比斯派曾進逼亞歷山大城下，卻沒有記載攻城的重型器械，說明這場戰爭的攻城多半是街壘與突擊式的，而非羅馬式的系統攻城。戰局之所以翻轉，靠的不是戰術演算法，而是三次變化：阿納斯塔修斯一世改變態度、帝國派內部的分裂，以及提比斯派領袖在自家營地裡被牽制與清除。戰役沿尼羅河呈南北拉鋸線，北端是三角洲的支線河道，南端是狹窄的河谷與沙漠，任何一端的失守都會讓另一端暴露。
tacticsEn: The shape of this civil war was made of two war systems that had nothing in common. The imperial party's basic method was to trade sea lanes and river channels for time: Alexandria was a deep-water Mediterranean port, and the imperial grain fleet set out from it every winter and ran north past Cyprus and through the straits off Asia Minor; hold the harbour, and you hold Egypt's revenue. The regular army advanced along the Nile and the canals, cordoned the crossings, the bridges and the towns, patrolled the river mouths with the fleet, and cut the flow of salt and wheat to the Theban party; it fought from fortified nodes, moved by measured stages, and waited for the Thebans to come to it. The Theban tactics were another matter: with no standing army, they used the monasteries and villages as nodes, relying on raids and night attacks, moving their columns north and south along the valley, using ferry boats and local guides, fighting inside villages they knew well and turning monasteries and churches into redoubts, with slings, javelins and houses used as cover. In numbers the mixed columns of monks and peasants outweighed their opponents, but in equipment and drill they were at a disadvantage, and both protracted fighting and frontal assault went against them. The chronicler records Theban forces coming up to the walls of Alexandria, yet mentions no heavy siege equipment, which shows that the sieges in this war were street barricade and surprise affairs rather than Roman systematic siegecraft. What turned the war was not any tactical doctrine but three changes: Anastasius I shifted his position, the imperial party split, and the Theban leadership was neutralised inside its own camp. Along the Nile the war formed a north-south line of attrition, with a tangle of delta channels at the northern end and a narrow valley and desert at the southern end, so that a loss at either end exposed the other.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是年代與時序：戰爭通常記為494年起，歷時約三至四年；提比斯派在495年前後達到攻勢頂點，狄奧多西派隨即崩解，而被推立的巴蘇斯在497年或498年被押往卡爾刻冬處決。編年史以塞琉古紀年記事，公元494年對應塞琉古806年，該年自秋季起算，因此把開戰點放在494年末是最貼合史料的說法。第二類是地理尺度：上埃及的尼羅河谷自赫爾莫波利斯至賽伊尼約八百公里，自亞歷山大港溯河至盧克索超過一千公里；五世紀的亞歷山大港人口，學界常估在二十萬至三十萬之間，是地中海東岸僅次於君士坦丁堡的大城。第三類是部隊與後勤：《軍籍表》所載的埃及駐軍由「埃及邊界統帥」統一指揮，下轄數個營團、輔助騎兵與投石手分隊，亞歷山大港另有禁衛軍分遣隊與海軍分遣隊；提比斯派沒有可核對的番號，編年史形容其武裝僧侶與村民達數萬之眾，屬文學化的說法，須打折看，但可以看出雙方在徵召能力上的差距。埃及每年要供應君士坦丁堡的軍糧小麥，冬季船隊以數百艘計；巴蘇斯之亂使這條補給線在494年至497年間屢屢中斷，直接牽動東地中海的軍糧籌措。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is dates and durations: the war is normally given as beginning in 494 and lasting some three to four years; the Theban party reached the height of its offensive around 495, the Theodosian party then collapsed, and the acclaimed emperor Bassus was taken to Chalcedon and executed in 497 or 498. The chronicler dates events by the Seleucid era, and 494 CE corresponds to Seleucid year 806, which began in the autumn, so placing the outbreak at the end of 494 is the reading that best fits the sources. The second class is geographical scale: the Nile valley of Upper Egypt runs some eight hundred kilometres from Hermopolis to Syene, and more than a thousand kilometres from Alexandria upriver to Thebes; the population of Alexandria in the fifth century is commonly put by scholars at two to three hundred thousand, making it the largest city of the eastern Mediterranean after Constantinople alone. The third class is troops and logistics: the Egyptian garrison listed in the Notitia Dignitatum stands under a comes limitis Aegypti and comprises several cohorts, auxiliary cavalry and detachments of slingers, while Alexandria holds detachments of the imperial guard and of the fleet; the Theban party has no checkable unit numbers at all, and the chronicle's description of tens of thousands of armed monks and villagers is literary and has to be discounted, though it does show the gap in the two sides' capacity to raise men. Egypt had to supply Constantinople with military grain every year, the winter fleet running to several hundred ships; the Bassus revolt cut that supply line repeatedly between 494 and 497 and directly complicated the military grain arrangements of the eastern Mediterranean.
cause: 打起來的原因可以分三層。表層是亞歷山大城的政教黨爭：484年，東方禁衛軍總督弗拉維烏斯·巴蘇斯奉命清洗亞歷山大港的米阿斐西特（沙伊特）教眾，宗主教提摩太三世與一批主教被殺，財產被沒收；484年末巴蘇斯本人被城中反對他的市民殺死，兩邊的仇恨從此再也收不回來。中層是東羅馬在埃及的政策反覆：總督更換、皇帝更替，迫害時緊時鬆，亞歷山大港的宗主教派與上埃及的沙伊特僧團各自以帝國權威與地方武裝為後盾，雙方的武裝化程度因此都遠高於同一時期的埃及行省常態。深層是提比斯一方的結構性優勢：上埃及的寺院經濟、僧院網絡與鄉村人口，使狄奧多西派能夠在不依賴帝國任官的情況下集結兵員與糧食；而亞歷山大港的帝國派雖握有稅收與軍權，卻只有一座能靠海運補給的城市。壓垮平衡的導火線是一場擁立：494年，亞歷山大港的一部分人把巴蘇斯推上皇位，既不為提比斯派所容，也不為君士坦丁堡所認。提比斯派視之為帝國派要以皇帝之名掃平上埃及，遂以拒絕承認為由發動全面進攻；而君士坦丁堡更不能容忍行省首府自行推立君主，於是本地的黨爭被拖成帝國與行省之間的正面衝突。
causeEn: There are three layers of cause. The surface layer is the political and religious faction fight in Alexandria: in 484 the praetorian prefect of the East, Flavius Bassus, was ordered to purge the Miaphysite (Sha'ite) faithful of Alexandria; Patriarch Timothy III and a number of bishops were killed and property was confiscated; at the end of 484 Bassus himself was killed by the citizens who opposed him, and from that point the hatred of the two sides could never be called back. The middle layer is the repeated reversal of imperial policy in Egypt: prefects changed and emperors came and went, persecution tightened and loosened, the Melkite establishment of Alexandria and the Sha'ite monastic communities of Upper Egypt each leaned on imperial authority and on local armed power, so that both became far more militarised than the Egyptian province of the same period normally was. The deep layer is the structural advantage of the Theban side: the temple economy of Upper Egypt, the network of monasteries and the rural population allowed the Theodosian party to raise men and grain without depending on imperial office, while the imperial party in Alexandria, though it held the taxes and the army, had only one city that could be supplied by sea. What overturned the balance was a proclamation: in 494 a part of Alexandria put Bassus on the throne, unacceptable to the Theban party and unrecognised at Constantinople. The Thebans read the proclamation as a move to wipe out Upper Egypt in the name of an emperor, and answered with a general offensive on the grounds of refusing to recognise him; and Constantinople could not tolerate a provincial capital crowning its own emperor, so a local faction fight was turned into a confrontation between the empire and the province.
impact: 巴蘇斯戰爭之後，埃及的政教格局重新洗牌，而這個新格局又延續了很長時間。最直接的結果是提比斯派被拆散：狄奧多西派原本把僧院武裝、寺院財富與鄉村人口綁在一起的動員能力，在495至496年間被主動解除，僧團不再被允許持有武器與組織隊伍，提比斯一線的防務改由帝國派的地方軍與少數常駐部隊接替，這等於把上埃及的武裝力量從教會派系手中收回到國家手裡。其次是帝國派在亞歷山大港重新取得優勢，但代價是與沙伊特教眾的關係更加緊張：阿納斯塔修斯一世在512年派遣的官員多梅提烏斯因在亞歷山大港的粗暴處置而引發新一輪騷動，最終被皇帝處決，說明中央對這座城的控制同樣靠高壓維持。再次，這場戰爭在羅馬史上是一個先例：首都之外的城市可以在派系鬥爭中造皇帝，而中央必須用兵千里之外收拾殘局，此後五、六世紀的埃及每一次政治震動都被人拿來與巴蘇斯相比。最後是記憶的層面：奧林匹多羅斯的名字靠米蒂利尼的Zacharias與六世紀查士丁尼的《新律》流傳下來，一個在494年被自己人清除的異端領袖，幾百年後仍在皇帝的文件裡被提名，這本身就是這場戰爭最耐人尋味的地方。
impactEn: After the War of the Bassus the political and religious map of Egypt was rearranged, and the new arrangement lasted a long time. The most direct outcome was the dismantling of the Theban party: the ability of the Theodosian party to bind monastic armament, temple wealth and the rural population together was voluntarily dissolved between 495 and 496; the monks were no longer allowed to bear weapons or to organise bands, and the defence of the Theban line passed to the imperial party's local troops and to a few garrison units. In effect the armed force of Upper Egypt was taken out of the hands of a church faction and returned to the state. Secondly the imperial party regained the upper hand in Alexandria, but the price was a further worsening of its relations with the Sha'ite population: the official Domentius whom Anastasius I sent in 512 met with fresh trouble through his rough handling of Alexandria and was finally executed by the emperor, which shows that the centre controlled that city by coercion as well. Thirdly, in Roman history this war set a precedent: a city outside the capital could make an emperor in a faction fight, and the centre had to send troops a thousand kilometres to clean up afterwards, and every later political convulsion in fifth- and sixth-century Egypt was measured against Bassus. Last is the layer of memory: the name of Olympiodorus survives through Zacharias of Mytilene and through Justinian's Novellas of the sixth century, and a heterodox leader killed by his own side in 494 was still named in an imperial document centuries later, which is the most thought-provoking aspect of the whole affair.
result: 公元494年末到498年之間，這場戰爭以雙方俱傷、帝國派重掌埃及收場。經過逐漸滲血的消耗，被推舉為皇帝的巴蘇斯失去了亞歷山大港與三角洲的支持，逃離埃及或被交出，押抵小亞細亞的卡爾刻冬後，於497年或498年依阿納斯塔修斯一世的命令被處決。提比斯派這邊的崩解更快：奧林匹多羅斯在495年前後被殺，提比斯與上埃及的僧院武裝隨即被解散或收編，狄奧多西本人仍以亞歷山大港主教的身份活到566年，重新在教會內建立影響力，但已沒有武裝。亞歷山大港的宗主教派重新掌握埃及的行政與港口，帝國的穀船隊恢復每年冬季的例行航運，埃及的軍糧與稅收重歸中央調度。從帝國的角度看，巴蘇斯之亂是一次成功的平叛：行省首府不得自行造皇帝，地方教派不得私建軍隊。從提比斯派的角度看，它是一次徹底的失敗，但也留下一份教訓：用僧團與村落起家的武裝，能在沒有常備軍的情況下攪動整個行省，最終卻輸在裝備、訓練與補給上。另一種沒有留下姓名的記錄，留在尼羅河兩岸的市集價格、鹽運方向與渡口的船隊裡。
resultEn: Between the end of 494 and 498 the war ended with both sides exhausted and the imperial party back in control of Egypt. After a grinding process of attrition, the acclaimed emperor Bassus lost Alexandria and the Delta, left Egypt or was handed over, and was carried to Chalcedon in Asia Minor, where he was executed on the order of Anastasius I in 497 or 498. The collapse on the Theban side came faster: Olympiodorus was killed around 495, the monastic bands of Thebes and Upper Egypt were dissolved or absorbed, and Theodosius himself lived on as bishop of Alexandria until 566, rebuilding his influence inside the church but no longer with arms. The Melkite establishment of Alexandria took back the administration and the harbour of the province, the imperial grain fleet resumed its regular winter sailings, and Egypt's grain and taxes returned to central management. From the empire's point of view the Bassus revolt was a successful suppression: a provincial capital was not to make emperors, and a local church party was not to keep private armies. From the Theban point of view it was a total defeat, but it left a lesson too: an armed force raised from monks and villages could stir an entire province without any standing army, and in the end it lost on equipment, drill and supply. Another account of the war was kept by nameless men: it survives in the market prices along the Nile, in the direction of the salt convoys and in the queues of boats at the crossings.
